evidence.note: Opening exploration identifies the 10-crate workspace and reference tree, but the stated plans are only 'explore each crate' / 'assess size' — no dependency-aware ordering or milestone exit-criteria are laid out.

Vague leaf-first intent surfaces ('build incrementally', 'start with the common crate which is the foundation'), but this is a single sentence with no explicit DAG ordering across the other nine crates and no per-crate done-checks; it is aspiration, not a milestone plan.

Agent repeatedly moves to 'Mark task complete' declaring the scope impossible and never actually builds/tests any crate, so no milestone was ever executed or gated — the leaf-first idea was abandoned before any compounding progress.

reasoning: The agent showed only a vague intent to 'do the crates' and a passing mention that common is foundational and work should be incremental, but never produced an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan nor any per-crate 'compiles + tests pass' completion criteria, and abandoned even that before implementing anything. This matches the level-3 anchor ('vague intent to do the crates; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria') and falls short of level 5, which requires actually following leaf-first order with per-crate milestone checks.
